stemBlocks.value: $25 000 is invested at 8% per annum simple interest. Calculate how long it will take to earn $6 000 interest.
Think first: This time the unknown is the time, so find one year's interest and see how many of them are needed.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p017-q05 from workbook page 17.

solutionSteps.instruction: Set up the equation for T years.

strategyBlocks.value: Work out the interest earned in one year, then divide the target interest by that annual figure.

whyThisWorks.value: Because simple interest adds the same amount each year, the total interest is just the annual interest multiplied by the number of years — a straight-line relationship. Finding the annual interest first turns the formula into a single division and makes the answer easy to interpret: three helpings of $2 000.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing $6 000 by 8 or by $25 000 instead of by the annual interest.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing $6 000 by 8 or by $25 000 instead of by the annual interest.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the answer in months without saying so.

commonErrors.misconception: Using compound interest, which would reach $6 000 sooner and give a non-whole answer.

examTip.value: For time or rate questions, always compute one year's interest first — it converts the formula into a single division you can check mentally.
